title: "Do NOT let a ___ fanatic see this": the gift idea warning
summary: Show one niche product or gift with a playful warning: don't let a certain kind of fan see it. AI writes the hooks and a cosy product photo prompt.
why: A trend tracker updated November 15, 2026 lists this as a rising format, up 75% on the week before: a niche product or gift idea with on-screen text like "Do NOT let a..." or "Don't show this to...", warning a certain kind of fanatic or mom who would want it right away.
steps: Pick one item that a specific type of person would love: a sourdough baker, a hockey parent, a houseplant collector.
Paste the main prompt to get hook lines, then pick the one that names your audience best.
Film the item close up for 5–8 seconds: a slow turn, a hand picking it up, the best detail last.
Put the hook on screen for the whole clip. Add one short line in the caption about what it is.

prompts.label: Main prompt: hook lines
prompts.text: Write 10 on-screen hooks for a short video showing this item: [describe the item]. Each hook starts with "Do NOT let a" or "Don't show this to" and names one specific type of person who would want it right away, like a [type of fan or hobby]. Keep each under 12 words and playful. Then suggest 3 close-up shots I can film in under 10 seconds. No hashtags, no emojis, no brand names.

prompts.label: Prompt: cosy product photo
prompts.text: Turn this photo of my item into a cosy holiday-season product shot. Keep the item exactly as it is, same shape, colours and details. Place it on a warm wooden table with soft window light, a knitted blanket and a few pine sprigs in the background, slightly out of focus. Vertical 9:16 with empty space at the top for on-screen text. No added text, no logos.

prompts.label: Variation: small business
prompts.text: I run [type of business] and sell [the product]. Write 8 "Do NOT let a ___ see this" hooks, each naming a different type of customer who would love it, like [a few real customer types]. Each under 12 words. Then write one honest caption line saying what it is and where to find it. Don't invent prices, discounts, reviews, sales numbers or fake urgency.

tips: The more specific the fan, the better. "Cross-country ski mom" beats "anyone who likes winter".
Save the best detail for the last second so people watch to the end.
Show the real item. If you use AI to make the photo nicer, keep the product exactly as it is.
Keep it a friendly tease, never a put-down of the people you name.
